supporting_observations.claim: The alerted periodic HTTPS activity is visible as proxy CONNECT attempts to update.chartmate-imaging.net at approximately five-minute intervals from 13:38 through 14:08 UTC; some attempts succeeded, while others returned 407 or 502.

The network connections are attributed by endpoint telemetry to PID 3416, running cmupdate.exe from Ben Carter's AppData\Local\ChartMate directory, rather than the inventory-listed Program Files location.

The observed hostname ends in chartmate-imaging.net, whereas the inventory lists update.chartmate-imaging.com as the approved updater destination. The hostname and executable location differences make attribution to the approved updater uncertain, but do not establish that the activity is malicious.

The cmupdate.exe process generated a file event targeting its own executable shortly after starting and making its first observed connection; this could be consistent with an update, but the record does not reveal what changed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT hostnames, status, and tunnel byte counts, but the evidence does not include the encrypted request contents or downloaded payload.
The supplied records do not provide the destination's resolved public IP, TLS certificate details, or domain ownership/reputation evidence.
The file event identifies the executable as a target but does not provide its resulting contents, hash, or signature.
claims_not_established: Whether update.chartmate-imaging.net is an authorized ChartMate domain or an unauthorized lookalike.
Whether the AppData executable is a legitimate ChartMate per-user updater or an impostor.
Whether the executable changed itself, and if so, what code or data changed.
Whether any malicious payload was delivered or executed during the HTTPS tunnels.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect the cmupdate.exe file and relevant versions, including cryptographic hashes, Authenticode signature status, and file metadata; compare them with a known-good ChartMate installer.
Obtain TLS certificate, DNS resolution, domain ownership, and reputation data for update.chartmate-imaging.net, and confirm the expected ChartMate update domain with the vendor or software owner.
Review endpoint file and process telemetry around the self-targeting file event and subsequent process termination to determine whether an update or replacement occurred.
Check proxy or network inspection data, if available, for the response contents or download details associated with the successful tunnels.
unrelated_findings: WS-BCARTER-01 made an SMB connection to FILE-HD-01 that was followed by an ANONYMOUS LOGON network logon; investigate separately because it is outside the alerted HTTPS activity. (T015-00253, T015-00257)
